name: The University of Tokyo
description: Japan's oldest and most prestigious national university, renowned for research excellence across the sciences, medicine, law, and humanities, with 19 Nobel laureates among its alumni and faculty.

name: Kyoto University
description: A leading national research university known for its tradition of academic freedom and independent research, especially strong in basic sciences, chemistry, and physics; alma mater of numerous Nobel laureates.

name: The University of Osaka
description: A major national research university (formerly Osaka University) known for strength in medicine, engineering, and the natural sciences, and for its large international student body.

name: Tohoku University
description: A top national research university especially recognized for materials science and engineering, and the first Japanese university to admit women and international students.

name: Institute of Science Tokyo
description: Japan's leading science and engineering-focused national university, formed in October 2024 by the merger of Tokyo Institute of Technology and Tokyo Medical and Dental University; renowned for engineering, dentistry, and applied sciences.

name: Nagoya University
description: A national research university known for strength in the natural sciences, with six Nobel Prize laureates in physics and chemistry among its faculty and alumni.

name: Hokkaido University
description: A national research university founded from Sapporo Agricultural College, known for agriculture, veterinary science, environmental studies, and a large international student community.

name: Kyushu University
description: One of Japan's leading national universities, a major research hub for engineering, sciences, and Asian studies located in Fukuoka on the southern island of Kyushu.

name: Waseda University
description: Japan's leading private university and top-ranked private institution in the country, known for political science, law, business, and having the largest international student population of any Japanese university.

name: Keio University
description: Japan's oldest private institution of higher learning, founded in 1858, highly regarded for business, economics, law, and medicine.

name: Hitotsubashi University
description: A prestigious small national university specializing exclusively in social sciences, especially renowned for economics, commerce, management, and law.

name: Osaka Metropolitan University
description: A large public university formed in 2022 from the merger of Osaka City University and Osaka Prefecture University, offering broad programs across sciences, engineering, medicine, and humanities.

name: Sophia University
description: A private Catholic university in central Tokyo known for its strong international outlook, foreign language education, and large proportion of English-taught programs for international students.

name: University of Tsukuba
description: A national university in the Tsukuba Science City known for interdisciplinary research, strong programs in sports science, and a comparatively large number of English-taught degree programs.

name: Hiroshima University
description: A comprehensive national university recognized for education, dentistry, and integrated sciences, and a hub of the Hiroshima region's international student community.

name: Kobe University
description: A national university especially well regarded for economics, business administration, and law, located in the port city of Kobe.

name: International Christian University
description: A small, highly selective private liberal arts university in Tokyo offering fully bilingual (Japanese/English) education, ranked Japan's top private university in several domestic rankings.

name: Ritsumeikan University
description: One of the largest private universities in Japan, with campuses in Kyoto, Shiga, and Osaka, known for its internationalization efforts and broad range of English-taught programs.

name: Doshisha University
description: A leading private university in Kyoto founded in 1875 with Christian roots, well known for law, economics, and international relations.

name: Meiji University
description: One of Japan's largest and most popular private universities, especially known for its law school heritage and strong programs in business, political science, and the arts.

name: Yokohama National University
description: A mid-sized national university near Tokyo known for engineering, business administration, and international social sciences, with close ties to industry in the Yokohama-Tokyo corridor.

name: Chiba University
description: A national university near Tokyo recognized for its programs in medicine, pharmaceutical sciences, horticulture, and engineering.
